content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp Creole with rice is a classic Creole dish that combines succulent shrimp, a flavorful tomato‑based sauce, onions, bell peppers, and a blend of spices, served over fluffy rice. The dish is known for its bright, slightly spicy taste and aromatic profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Creole cuisine originated in Louisiana, USA, blending French, Spanish, African, and Caribbean influences.
Tomatoes in the sauce are often replaced with tomato paste to intensify flavor and thickness.
Traditionally the dish is made with long‑grain white rice, though brown or wild rice are also used today.
When cooked together with the sauce, the rice creates a hearty jambalaya‑style stew.
Shrimp Creole is popular throughout the Southern United States and the Caribbean.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Shrimp provide a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many animal proteins, shrimp contain very little saturated fat.

items.title: Rich in selenium
items.content: Selenium supports immune function and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Shrimp are a good source of vitamin B12 and niacin, important for nervous system health and metabolism.

items.title: Tomato antioxidants
items.content: The tomato base supplies lycopene, a potent antioxidant with anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to shrimp, ranging from mild skin irritation to severe anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Traditional Creole sauce can be high in salt; adjust seasoning to keep sodium intake in check.

items.title: Additives in prepared sauces
items.content: If using store‑bought tomato paste or sauce, check for preservatives and artificial flavors.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sauté onion, bell pepper, and garlic, add tomatoes and spices (paprika, cayenne, thyme) and simmer until thick. Stir in peeled shrimp and cook 3‑5 minutes until pink. Serve over cooked rice, garnished with fresh herbs and a lime wedge.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in freezer‑safe bags for 1‑2 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat gently on the stove.
